alignments.note: Conditional particle to the word introducing the English clause (rule 40). Not rule 65's concessive cluster: no καί stands with it.
Postpositive δέ realized by the fronted *but*; rule 15 permits the reordering. Kept separate from εἰ under rule 2, the two particles having separate English words.

One Greek verb expanded into the English phrase *have respect of persons*; the supplied subject *ye* and the light auxiliary *have* ride inside under rules 7 and 9, and the *of persons* completes the idiom rather than answering to any Greek preposition, so rule 36 is not in question. Rule 91 decides the head: it is the word the corpus spends on the προσωπολημπτ- lexeme, not the phrase's formal English head, and the ASV renders that family *respect of persons* throughout — the same wording rule 84 lists for the privative ἀπροσωπολήμπτως, where the noun after *without* is *respect*. A head on *persons* is the competing reading, πρόσωπον being the more direct gloss of the compound's first element; it is refused because rule 91 replaces that compositional argument with what the corpus spends on the lemma, and *respect* is the word carrying the sense of partiality. Rule 73 is not the case here, the Greek expressing one token rather than a verb-plus-noun pair.
Accusative object to its noun; rule 2 keeps it separate from the verb even though the ASV reorders.
Inflected verb with its supplied subject; rule 9 heads on the lexical verb, not the pronoun.
Passive participle with its periphrastic *being*; rule 9 heads on the participle. The participle keeps its own English clause and no juncture is supplied, so rules 88 and 98 are not in question.
Agentive preposition to *by* (rule 36). This is an expressed proper preposition rendered by a single word, not a complex frame, so rules 67 and 95 are not in question.
Article to *the* (rule 19); the preposition is expressed and takes its own word, so no case preposition rides with the article under rule 21.
Noun stands alone, the determiner having gone to its own article (rules 13 and 26).
Comparative adverb to *as*; no correlative καί follows, so rule 82 is not in question.
Predicate noun to *transgressors*; the Greek is anarthrous and the ASV supplies no determiner, so rule 58 has nothing to place.

review_notes: Reviewed; the accepted alignment stands unchanged. Only the notes were strengthened, chiefly on s003.
All 11 source and 17 target ids partitioned exactly once; every unit is aligned with nonempty arrays and heads drawn from their own arrays.

No unrepresented or added units are warranted: every source token has an English realization and every English token answers to a source token. Nothing is displaced into a neighbouring verse (rule 37) and the verse carries no fallback-exclusion mark (rule 97).

s003 is the only materially contested head. *respect* over *persons* is argued from rule 91's operational test rather than from rule 17's meaning-bearing clause alone; the note names the competing reading and why it is refused. If a chapter conventions log records JAS.2.1's προσωπολημψίαις → *respect of persons* headed otherwise, that unit governs and this one should be brought into line with it.

τοῦ νόμου was audited under rule 13 and split: the expressed ὑπό takes *by*, so the article takes a bare *the* and the noun stands alone rather than the article carrying a case preposition under rule 21.
s003's *of* is idiom-internal, not a case preposition and not a realization of any Greek preposition, so rule 36 does not pull it out of the unit.
